3.text: And [by] the even [number] and the odd

4.text: And [by] the night when it passes,

5.text: Is there [not] in [all] that an oath [sufficient] for one of perception?<sup foot_note="228227">1</sup>

footnotes.228227: - Based upon the following verses, what has been sworn to by Allāh is that He will certainly punish the disbelievers.

6.text: Have you not considered how your Lord dealt with ʿAad -

7.text: [With] Iram<sup foot_note="228228">1</sup> - who had lofty pillars,<sup foot_note="228229">2</sup>

footnotes.228228: Another name for the first people of ʿAad, to whom Prophet Hūd was sent.

8.text: The likes of whom had never been created in the land?

9.text: And [with] Thamūd, who carved out the rocks in the valley?

10.text: And [with] Pharaoh, owner of the stakes?<sup foot_note="228230">1</sup>

11.text: [All of] whom oppressed within the lands

13.text: So your Lord poured upon them a scourge of punishment.

14.text: Indeed, your Lord is in observation.

15.text: And as for man, when his Lord tries him and [thus] is generous to him and favors him, he says, "My Lord has honored me."<sup foot_note="228231">1</sup>

footnotes.228231: - He is proud rather than grateful, attributing the favor to his own merit.

16.text: But when He tries him and restricts his provision, he says, "My Lord has humiliated me."

17.text: No!<sup foot_note="228232">1</sup> But you do not honor the orphan

footnotes.228232: - It is not like you imagine. Rather, Allāh tries people through prosperity and hardship and rewards both gratitude and patience with honor in the Hereafter.

18.text: And you do not encourage one another to feed the poor.

19.text: And you consume inheritance, devouring [it] altogether,<sup foot_note="228233">1</sup>

footnotes.228233: - Not caring whether it is lawful or unlawful.

20.text: And you love wealth with immense love.

21.text: No! When the earth has been leveled - pounded and crushed

22.text: And your Lord has come<sup foot_note="228234">1</sup> and the angels, rank upon rank,

footnotes.228234: - To pass judgement. See footnote to 2:19.

23.text: And brought [within view], that Day, is Hell - that Day, man will remember, but how [i.e., what good] to him will be the remembrance?

24.text: He will say, "Oh, I wish I had sent ahead [some good] for my life."<sup foot_note="228235">1</sup>

footnotes.228235: - The everlasting life of the Hereafter.

25.text: So on that Day, none will punish [as severely] as His punishment,

26.text: And none will bind [as severely] as His binding [of the evildoers].
